title: Rollout policy editor: Auto-rollback on SLO breach section (thresholds, windows, templates, guardrails UX)
creator: Paula Mendes
description:
## Context
We’re adding auto-rollback / auto-pause actions triggered by SLO breaches during canary + A/B rollouts. This ticket covers the *policy editor UX* for configuring those behaviors in Console.

This section must make it easy to:
- pick safe defaults (templates) for common tiers
- understand what signals are used (latency p95/p99, error rate, saturation where eligible)
- configure thresholds + evaluation windows without causing flapping/oscillation
- see inline validation + warnings based on safe bounds enforced by the policy engine

The policy model is being implemented in ENG-4822 and will enforce hard limits; design should reflect those limits and guide users before they hit “Save”.

## Users / personas
1) Platform engineer / service owner
- Owns a route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions) and wants rollouts to self-mitigate regressions.
- Often doesn’t know SRE burn-rate terminology; needs plain-language guidance.

2) SRE / on-call
- Wants predictable behavior (no rollback storms) and clear suppression/override visibility.
- Needs policy changes to be auditable and “safe by default”.

3) Enterprise admin
- Wants consistency across many services/teams; prefers templates and locked defaults.

## Goals
- Provide an “Auto-mitigation” section inside Rollout Policy Editor that supports:
  - Enable/disable automatic actions on SLO breach
  - Action choice: Pause rollout vs Rollback to last known-good vs Shift traffic back to baseline (A/B)
  - Configure evaluation windows (fast burn + slow burn) + minimum sample size gating
  - Templates per customer tier (Self-serve / Dedicated / Private) with editable overrides
  - Inline warnings and constraints to prevent unsafe configs
  - Clear explanation of what happens when monitors are missing/stale

## Non-goals
- Designing the audit log timeline UI (tracked in DES-944)
- Designing incident-bot Slack notifications
- Model quality regression / eval-based rollback signals

## Proposed IA / section layout (policy editor)
### Section header: “Auto-mitigation (SLO-based)” (new)
- Toggle: “Automatically pause/rollback when SLOs breach”
- Short helper text: “Uses latency and error-rate SLO monitors scoped to this rollout (route/model/version/region/tier).”
- Link: “View eligible monitors” (opens a read-only panel/list; if not available, link to docs)

### 1) Template selector (shown when enabled)
- Dropdown / radio cards:
  - Recommended (Tier default)
  - Conservative
  - Aggressive (with warning + ‘not recommended for production’ tooltip)
  - Custom
- When a template is selected, fields below populate; any edits auto-switch to “Custom” with a subtle ‘modified’ badge.
- Include “Reset to template” action.

Template preview (inline summary):
- “Action: Pause”
- “Fast window: 5m / Slow window: 30m”
- “Min requests: 1,000 (per window)”
- “Debounce/holdoff: 10m after action”

### 2) Action on breach
- Primary select: Pause | Rollback | Shift traffic back to baseline
- Secondary behaviors (collapsed by default):
  - “When action executes, require manual approval to resume rollout” (checkbox)
  - “Notify Slack channel” (if channel config is part of policy; otherwise link to oncall setup)

Inline guidance:
- Pause: safest default; prevents further exposure
- Rollback: recommended for canary/staged upgrades where last known-good exists
- Shift-to-baseline: recommended for A/B tests with baseline stable

### 3) Breach evaluation (windows + burn)
Because “burn-rate” is jargon, UI should be phrased as:
- “Detect fast regressions” (fast window)
- “Confirm sustained regressions” (slow window)

Fields:
- Fast window duration (dropdown: 2m, 5m, 10m)
- Slow window duration (dropdown: 15m, 30m, 60m)
- Condition: “Trigger action when *both* windows breach” (fixed; explain rationale to avoid flapping)
- Debounce / holdoff after action (dropdown: 5m, 10m, 30m)

If the backend exposes the canonical fast/slow options only, the UI must constrain to those options (no free-form).

### 4) Minimum traffic / sample size gate
- “Only act if enough traffic is present to be confident”
- Field: “Minimum requests per window” (numeric)
- Optional: “Minimum error count” for error-rate-based triggers (if supported)

Inline warning states:
- If set too low: “Higher chance of false positives during low traffic.”
- If set too high: “May delay mitigation; breaches could go unmitigated.”

### 5) Signals (what SLOs can trigger)
A simple checklist (if policy supports selecting signals; otherwise read-only list).
- Latency p95
- Latency p99
- Error rate (5xx)
- Saturation (if eligible)

For each signal:
- Show the threshold source: “From SLO monitor” vs “Override threshold” (prefer “From monitor” default)
- If overrides are allowed:
  - Provide a guarded override control with a “Restore monitor threshold” action
  - Display “Effective threshold” and “Monitor threshold” side-by-side

### 6) Missing / stale monitor behavior
This is critical for safety.
- Read-only statement of system behavior (aligned with eng/SRE decision):
  - “If a required monitor is missing or stale, auto-mitigation will not execute and the rollout will continue.” OR “will pause” (TBD)
- Visual callout:
  - If editor detects missing monitors (via API): show warning and recommended next step (“Create monitor”, “See runbook”).

### 7) Suppressions / overrides (visibility only in editor)
Policy editor should show current suppression state and how to request it.
- “Suppression windows are admin-only.”
- If user lacks permission: show locked row with tooltip “Requires Rollouts Admin”.
- If user has permission: link/button “Request suppression” opens admin modal (modal design can be covered elsewhere; this ticket focuses on the policy editor section placement and copy.)

## Guardrails + inline validation requirements
- Hard bounds (policy engine enforced) must be surfaced early with inline errors:
  - windows must be within allowed set
  - fast window must be < slow window
  - debounce/holdoff minimum and maximum
  - minimum requests threshold range
  - action restrictions by rollout type (e.g., “Rollback requires previous version pinned”)
- Soft warnings (non-blocking) for risky combos:
  - Aggressive template in prod env / top-tier routes
  - Rollback enabled without a “resume requires approval” checkbox
  - Custom overrides diverging from tier defaults

Validation copy must be explicit about outcomes:
- “This configuration may cause repeated rollbacks (“flapping”) during noisy telemetry.”
- “This configuration may never trigger during low traffic.”

## Edge cases to design for
- Route has multiple regions selected; show whether policy applies per region vs global (copy + tooltip)
- A/B rollout without a clean ‘last known-good’ version (disable rollback option, explain why)
- Missing monitors at save time (block vs warn; TBD by SRE/eng). Provide UX for both:
  - Blocking: inline error and ‘create monitor’ link
  - Warning-only: yellow banner + ‘save anyway’ confirmation
- Staging vs prod: show environment badges; warn when enabling for prod
- RBAC: viewers can see policy but cannot edit; provide read-only rendering of section

## Content / copy notes (tone)
- Prefer plain language (avoid “burn rate” unless parenthetical)
- Make safety intent explicit: “Auto-mitigation is a safety rail; it trades faster containment for potential false positives.”
- Always include links to runbook + docs

## Analytics / success signals (instrumentation hooks)
- Track template selection rate and % switching to custom
- Track save failures due to validation (which rule)
- Track enablement rate by tier and rollout type

## Deliverables
- Figma: policy editor section (enabled/disabled, templates, custom edits, read-only state)
- Component spec: validation states (error/warn/info), copy strings, and gating rules
- Hand-off notes for ENG-4822 (field constraints, which values are selectable vs free-form)

## Open questions (need alignment)
1) Missing/stale monitors: fail-open (no action) vs fail-closed (pause)? SRE decision needed.
2) Do we allow per-signal enable/disable (e.g., latency only) in MVP, or fixed set?
3) Do we allow overrides of SLO thresholds in policy editor, or only via SLO config tooling?
4) Should ‘Rollback’ be hidden in A/B policies, or shown disabled with explanation?

## References
- PM defaults/templates: PM-618
- MVP scope: PM-612
- Eng schema/validation: ENG-4822
- Audit log detail UI: DES-944
- Confluence PRD: auto-rollback-slo-integration PRD
- Slack: product thread clarifying MVP (pause vs rollback semantics)
acceptance_criteria: Policy editor has a dedicated “Auto-mitigation (SLO-based)” section with enable toggle and clear helper copy.
Template selector supports tier default + conservative/aggressive + custom, with “reset to template”.
User can choose action on breach (pause/rollback/shift-to-baseline) with appropriate disablement for unsupported rollout types.
Evaluation windows, minimum sample size, and debounce/holdoff are editable within constrained options; invalid configs show inline errors before save.
Inline warnings communicate risk of flapping/false positives and link to runbook/docs.
RBAC read-only state is designed (view vs edit) and suppression controls are clearly admin-only.
Edge states for missing/stale monitors are represented (banner + recommended next step), pending final SRE behavior decision.

comments: 2026-02-11 — Paula Mendes: PM-618 will define template names + tier defaults. Please keep ‘Aggressive’ behind a warning and consider gating in prod. MVP must include pause + rollback; shift-to-baseline is nice-to-have if it’s already in the policy model.

2026-02-13 — Sean Gallagher: Strong preference for dual-window confirmation + min sample size in UI (no free-form). We should not encourage threshold overrides unless we can ensure alignment with SLO ownership; ideally show ‘from monitor’ only for MVP.

2026-02-18 — Jordan Lee: Policy engine will likely enforce discrete allowed windows + hard min/max for sample sizes and holdoff. I’ll share exact enums once finalized so design can match (avoid user entering unsupported values).

2026-02-20 — Kenji Nakamura: Draft IA complete. Next step is Figma frames for (1) disabled state, (2) template selected, (3) custom edits + warnings, (4) missing monitor banner. Waiting on SRE answer for fail-open vs fail-closed on missing monitors.

2026-02-24 — Allison Grant: Please include label/cardinality note somewhere in help text if we expose per-region/per-tier scoping; users often misunderstand scope. Tooltip suggestion: “Evaluations run per (region,tier,route,model version) scope.”

2026-02-26 — Marissa Cole: Looks directionally good. Keep the copy short; advanced settings should be collapsed. Also ensure ‘Rollback’ copy explains it reverts traffic to last known-good model version and records audit event.
